sentences.text:
Smt. Renu And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21
July, 2023
Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav

Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:146042
Court No. - 71
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 7811 of 2023
Applicant :- Smt. Renu And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Lalit Kumar Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard Sri Lalit Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as well as perused the material available on record.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.171 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC, Police Station- Kotwali,
District- Mathura, during pendency of investigation.

3. As per F.I.R. version, there are fourteen persons named in the F.I.R. and allegations against them is that applicants and other persons have taken gold loan by mortgaging the duplicate gold and after taking forged appraisal certificate from the authorised firm M/s Dev Jewelers and when Bank re-appraisal mortgaged gold, it was found that the mortgaged gold are duplicate and its market value is zero.

It is further alleged that the Bank has demanded back his loan amount to the Smt. Renu And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137704045/
1 applicants and others, they did not returned the loan amount to the Bank.

entities.text: Smt. Renu And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further alleged that applicant no.1 has taken gold loan of Rs.9,82,000/-, applicant no.2 has taken gold loan of Rs.14,06,000/- and applicant no.3 has taken gold loan of Rs.12,75,000/- on 27.08.2021.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicants are bonafide loan holders and they have no role of cheating and have not committed any fraud as alleged in the F.I.R..
He submitted that the Bank had given loan to the applicants after examining the gold by the Bank through its authorised dealer.

Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that co-accused Sushil Kumar Chaturvedi and Shishu Pal Singh have been granted anticipatory bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 20.05.2022 and 15.07.2022 passed in Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application No.3939 of 2022 and 5145 of 2022, copy of the same are annexed as Annexure No.3 to the affidavit.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application No.3939 of 2022 and 5145 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He further submitted the applicants have no criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph no.26 of the affidavit.

Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that applicants have apprehension of imminent arrest and in case, applicants are released on anticipatory bail, they will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate with the trial.

5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant and has submitted that the applicants have committed fraud with the Bank in obtaining loan, therefore, therefore, keeping in view the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicants, they are not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail.
The apprehension of the applicants is not founded on any material on record.
Only on the basis of imaginary fear, anticipatory bail cannot be granted.
6. From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicants.

7. After having very carefully examined, the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicants and perused the material brought on record, there is no justification for granting anticipatory bail to the applicants.
Accordingly, the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail is hereby refused.

8. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submitted that directions may be given to the court below to consider the regular bail application of the applicant, expeditiously, in accordance with law.

9. In view of the above, considering the aforesaid alternative prayer made by learned counsel for the applicant, it is directed that the applicants shall surrender before the concerned court below, and in case, a regular bail application is filed, the same be heard and decided by the court below,
expeditiously, in accordance with law.
10. With the above directions, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally.

Order Date :- 21.7.2023 Krishna*
